# Bulsara (crater)

**Bulsara** is a crater on [Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(planet) "Mercury (planet)"). Its name was adopted by the [International Astronomical Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union") (IAU) in May 2024, for British musician Farrokh Bulsara, better known as [Freddie Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Mercury "Freddie Mercury"), lead vocalist and pianist of the rock band [Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_(band) "Queen (band)"), who lived from 1946 to 1991.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Bulsara is located between [Rembrandt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rembrandt_(crater) "Rembrandt (crater)") to the east and [Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lennon_(crater) "Lennon (crater)") to the west. Together with crater [Joplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joplin_(crater) "Joplin (crater)"), Lennon and Bulsara form a line of nearly equally spaced craters.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Distribution of named [craters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") in the [Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System") as of 2017[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_craters_on_Mercury&action=edit)[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Moon-Craterlist-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mars-Craterlist-4)[[5]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-5)[[a]](#cite_note-WGPSN-Dropped-6)

This is a list of named [craters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") on [Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(planet) "Mercury (planet)"), the [innermost planet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_planets "Inner planets") of the [Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System") *(for other features, see [list of geological features on Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_geological_features_on_Mercury "List of geological features on Mercury"))*.[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2) Most Mercurian craters [are named after](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetary_nomenclature "Planetary nomenclature") famous writers, artists and composers. According to the rules by IAU's [Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_Group_for_Planetary_System_Nomenclature "Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature"), all new craters must be named after an artist that was famous for more than fifty years, and dead for more than three years, before the date they are named.[[6]](#cite_note-Ritzel-7) Craters larger than 250 km in diameter are referred to as "basins" *(also see [§ Terminology](#Terminology))*.[[7]](#cite_note-8)[[8]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Categories-9)

As of 2025[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_craters_on_Mercury&action=edit), there are 444 named Mercurian craters,[[2]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mercury-Craterlist-2) a small fraction of the total number of named Solar System craters, most of which are [lunar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_the_Moon "List of craters on the Moon"), [Martian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Mars "List of craters on Mars") and [Venerian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Venus "List of craters on Venus") craters.[[3]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Moon-Craterlist-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Mars-Craterlist-4)[[5]](#cite_note-Gazetteer-Venus-Craterlist-5)[[a]](#cite_note-WGPSN-Dropped-6)

Other, non-planetary bodies with numerous named craters include [Callisto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callisto_(moon) "Callisto (moon)") ([141](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Callisto "List of craters on Callisto")), [Ganymede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganymede_(moon) "Ganymede (moon)") ([131](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Ganymede "List of craters on Ganymede")), [Rhea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhea_(moon) "Rhea (moon)") (128), [Vesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4_Vesta "4 Vesta") (90), [Ceres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceres_(dwarf_planet) "Ceres (dwarf planet)") (90), [Dione](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dione_(moon) "Dione (moon)") (73), [Iapetus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iapetus_(moon) "Iapetus (moon)") (58), [Enceladus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enceladus_(moon) "Enceladus (moon)") (53), [Tethys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tethys_(moon) "Tethys (moon)") (50) and [Europa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europa_(moon) "Europa (moon)") ([41](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_on_Europa "List of craters on Europa")). For a full list, *see [List of craters in the Solar System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_craters_in_the_Solar_System "List of craters in the Solar System")*.

![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/Joplin_crater_EN0235254321M.jpg/330px-Joplin_crater_EN0235254321M.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)

**Joplin** is a crater on [Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(planet) "Mercury (planet)"). Its name was adopted by the [International Astronomical Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union") (IAU) in 2012, after the American composer [Scott Joplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Joplin "Scott Joplin").[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Joplin's [peak ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peak_ring "Peak ring") is relatively small compared to the crater diameter and it is offset from the center. It is one of 110 peak ring basins on Mercury.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Joplin is located about half-way between the prominent crater [Debussy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debussy_(crater) "Debussy (crater)") and the crater [Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lennon_(crater) "Lennon (crater)"). It is south of the crater [Travers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travers_(crater) "Travers (crater)"). Together with crater [Bulsara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulsara_(crater) "Bulsara (crater)") (named after [Freddie Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Mercury "Freddie Mercury")), Lennon and Joplin form a line of nearly equally spaced craters.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

**Aaron Copland** ([/ˈkoʊplənd/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English") [*KOHP-lənd*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key");[[1]](#cite_note-1)[[2]](#cite_note-2) November 14, 1900 – December 2, 1990) was an American composer, critic, writer, teacher, pianist, and conductor of his own and other American music. Copland was referred to by his peers and critics as the "Dean of American Music". The open, slowly changing harmonies in much of his music are typical of what many consider the sound of American music, evoking the vast American landscape and pioneer spirit. He is best known for the works he wrote in the 1930s and 1940s in a deliberately accessible style often referred to as "populist" and which he called his "vernacular" style.[[3]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPollack1999186-3) Works in this vein include the ballets *[Appalachian Spring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appalachian_Spring "Appalachian Spring")*, *[Billy the Kid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_the_Kid_(ballet) "Billy the Kid (ballet)")* and *[Rodeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodeo_(ballet) "Rodeo (ballet)")*, his *[Fanfare for the Common Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanfare_for_the_Common_Man "Fanfare for the Common Man")* and [Third Symphony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symphony_No._3_(Copland) "Symphony No. 3 (Copland)"). In addition to his ballets and orchestral works, he produced music in many other genres, including chamber music, vocal works, opera, and film scores.

After some initial studies with composer [Rubin Goldmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubin_Goldmark "Rubin Goldmark"), Copland traveled to Paris, where he first studied with [Isidor Philipp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isidor_Philipp "Isidor Philipp") and [Paul Vidal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Vidal "Paul Vidal"), then with noted pedagogue [Nadia Boulanger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadia_Boulanger "Nadia Boulanger"). He studied three years with Boulanger, whose eclectic approach to music inspired his own broad taste. Determined upon his return to the U.S. to make his way as a full-time composer, Copland gave lecture-recitals, wrote works on commission and did some teaching and writing. But he found that composing orchestral music in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modernism_(music) "Modernism (music)") style, which he had adopted while studying abroad, was unprofitable, particularly in light of the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression"). He shifted in the mid-1930s to a more accessible musical style that mirrored the German idea of *[Gebrauchsmusik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gebrauchsmusik "Gebrauchsmusik")* ("music for use"), music that could serve utilitarian and artistic purposes. During the Depression years, he traveled extensively to Europe, Africa, and Mexico, formed an important friendship with Mexican composer [Carlos Chávez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Chávez "Carlos Chávez"), and began composing his signature works.

During the late 1940s, Copland became aware that [Stravinsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stravinsky "Stravinsky") and other fellow composers had begun to study [Arnold Schoenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold_Schoenberg "Arnold Schoenberg")'s use of [twelve-tone (serial) techniques](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelve-tone_technique "Twelve-tone technique"). After he had been exposed to the works of French composer [Pierre Boulez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Boulez "Pierre Boulez"), he incorporated serial techniques into his *Piano Quartet* (1950), *Piano Fantasy* (1957), *[Connotations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connotations_(Copland) "Connotations (Copland)")* for orchestra (1961), and *[Inscape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inscape_(Copland) "Inscape (Copland)")* for orchestra (1967). Unlike Schoenberg, Copland used his tone rows in much the same fashion as his tonal material—as sources for melodies and harmonies, rather than as complete statements in their own right, except for crucial events from a structural point of view. From the 1960s onward, Copland's activities turned more from composing to conducting. He became a frequent guest conductor of orchestras in the U.S. and the UK and made a series of recordings of his music, primarily for [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records").

## Life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Aaron_Copland&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life")]

### Early years

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Aaron_Copland&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early years")]

Aaron Copland was born in [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"), New York, on November 14, 1900.[[4]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPollack199915-4) He was the youngest of five children in a [Conservative Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Jewish "Conservative Jewish") immigrant family of [Lithuanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuanian_Jews "Lithuanian Jews") origin.[[5]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECoplandPerlis198419-5) While emigrating from Russia to the United States, Copland's father, Harris Morris Copland, lived and worked in Scotland for two to three years to pay for his boat fare to the United States. It was there that Copland's father may have [Anglicized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglicized "Anglicized") his surname "Kaplan" to "Copland", though Copland himself believed for many years that the change had been caused by an [Ellis Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellis_Island "Ellis Island") immigration official when his father entered the country.[[4]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPollack199915-4)[[6]](#cite_note-Cone-6) Copland was unaware until late in his life that the family name had been Kaplan, his parents having never told him.[[6]](#cite_note-Cone-6) Throughout his childhood, Copland and his family lived above his parents' Brooklyn shop, H. M. Copland's, at 628 Washington Avenue (which Aaron later called "a kind of neighborhood [Macy's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macy's "Macy's")"),[[7]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPollack199916-7)[[8]](#cite_note-8) on the corner of Dean Street and Washington Avenue,[[9]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTERoss2007266-9) and most of the children helped out in the store. His father was a staunch Democrat. The family members were active in [Congregation Baith Israel Anshei Emes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congregation_Baith_Israel_Anshei_Emes "Congregation Baith Israel Anshei Emes"), where Aaron celebrated his [bar mitzvah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_mitzvah "Bar mitzvah"),[[10]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPollack199926-10) for which he studied under [Israel Goldfarb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Goldfarb "Israel Goldfarb").[[11]](#cite_note-jmrc-11) Not especially athletic, the sensitive young man became an avid reader and often read [Horatio Alger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horatio_Alger "Horatio Alger") stories on his front steps.[[12]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith195315-12)

Copland's father had no musical interest. His mother, Sarah Mittenthal Copland, sang, played the piano, and arranged music lessons for her children.[[13]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPollack199919-13) Copland had four older siblings: two brothers, Ralph and Leon, and two sisters, Laurine and Josephine.[[14]](#cite_note-14)[[15]](#cite_note-15) Of his siblings, his oldest brother Ralph was the most advanced musically; he was proficient on the violin. Laurine had the strongest connection with Aaron; she gave him his first piano lessons, promoted his musical education, and supported him in his musical career.[[13]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPollack199919-13) A student at the Metropolitan Opera School and frequent opera-goer, Laurine also brought home [libretti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libretti "Libretti") for Aaron to study.[[16]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith195317-16) Copland attended [Boys High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boys_High_School_(Brooklyn) "Boys High School (Brooklyn)") and in the summer went to various camps. Most of his early exposure to music was at Jewish weddings and ceremonies, and occasional family musicales.[[10]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPollack199926-10)

Copland began writing songs at the age of eight and a half.[[17]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECoplandPerlis198422-17) His earliest notated music, about seven bars he wrote when age 11, was for an opera scenario he created and called *Zenatello*.[[17]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECoplandPerlis198422-17)[[18]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPollack199932-18) From 1913 to 1917 he took piano lessons with Leopold Wolfsohn, who taught him the standard classical fare.[[17]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECoplandPerlis198422-17) Copland's first public music performance was at a [Wanamaker's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wanamaker's "Wanamaker's") recital.[[19]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith195318-19)[[20]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECoplandPerlis198423-20) By age 15, after attending a concert by Polish composer-pianist [Ignacy Jan Paderewski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ignacy_Jan_Paderewski "Ignacy Jan Paderewski"), Copland decided to become a composer.[[21]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPollack199933-21) At 16, he heard his first symphony, at the [Brooklyn Academy of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Academy_of_Music "Brooklyn Academy of Music").[[22]](#cite_note-nyclgbtsites.org-22) After attempts to further his music study from a [correspondence course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Correspondence_course "Correspondence course"), C

**George Gershwin** ([/ˈɡɜːrʃ.wɪn/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); born **Jacob Gershwine**; September 26, 1898 – July 11, 1937) was an American composer and pianist whose compositions spanned [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz"), [popular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_music "Popular music") and [classical music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_music "Classical music"). Among his best-known works are the songs "[Swanee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swanee_(song) "Swanee (song)")" (1919) and "[Fascinating Rhythm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fascinating_Rhythm "Fascinating Rhythm")" (1924), the orchestral compositions *[Rhapsody in Blue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhapsody_in_Blue "Rhapsody in Blue")* (1924) and *[An American in Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An_American_in_Paris "An American in Paris")* (1928) and his *[Piano Concerto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concerto_in_F_(Gershwin) "Concerto in F (Gershwin)")* (1925), the [jazz standards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_standard "Jazz standard") "[Embraceable You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embraceable_You "Embraceable You")" (1928) and "[I Got Rhythm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Got_Rhythm "I Got Rhythm")" (1930) and the opera *[Porgy and Bess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porgy_and_Bess "Porgy and Bess")* (1935), which included the hit "[Summertime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summertime_(George_Gershwin_song) "Summertime (George Gershwin song)")". His *[Of Thee I Sing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Of_Thee_I_Sing "Of Thee I Sing")* (1931) was the first [musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_theater "Musical theater") to win the [Pulitzer Prize for Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Drama "Pulitzer Prize for Drama"), although as composer, he did not participate in reception of the award.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Gershwin studied piano under [Charles Hambitzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Hambitzer "Charles Hambitzer") and composition with [Rubin Goldmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubin_Goldmark "Rubin Goldmark"), [Henry Cowell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Cowell "Henry Cowell"), and [Joseph Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Brody "Joseph Brody"). He began his career as a [song plugger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_plugger "Song plugger") but soon started composing Broadway theater works with his brother [Ira Gershwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ira_Gershwin "Ira Gershwin") and with [Buddy DeSylva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_DeSylva "Buddy DeSylva"). He moved to Paris, intending to study with [Nadia Boulanger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadia_Boulanger "Nadia Boulanger"), but she refused him, afraid that rigorous classical study would ruin his jazz-influenced style; [Maurice Ravel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Ravel "Maurice Ravel") voiced similar objections when Gershwin inquired about studying with him.[[2]](#cite_note-Greenberg-2) He subsequently composed *An American in Paris*, returned to New York City and wrote *Porgy and Bess* with Ira and [DuBose Heyward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DuBose_Heyward "DuBose Heyward"). Initially a commercial failure, it came to be considered one of the most important American operas of the 20th century and an American cultural classic.

Gershwin moved to Hollywood and composed several film scores. He died in 1937, only 38 years old, of a brain tumor.[[3]](#cite_note-3) His compositions have been adapted for use in film and television, with many becoming jazz standards.

## Life and career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=George_Gershwin&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life and career")]

### Ancestors

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=George_Gershwin&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Ancestors")]

Gershwin's parents were both Jewish immigrants from the Russian Empire. His paternal grandfather, Jakov Gershovitz, was born in [Odessa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odessa "Odessa"), then part of the [Russian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Empire "Russian Empire"), and had served for 25 years as a mechanic for the [Imperial Russian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Russian_Army "Imperial Russian Army") to earn the right of free travel and residence as a Jew, finally retiring near [Saint Petersburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Petersburg "Saint Petersburg"), Russia. Jakov's teenage son, Moishe, George Gershwin's father, worked as a leather cutter for women's shoes. George's mother, Roza Bruskina, was born in [Saint Petersburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Petersburg "Saint Petersburg").[[4]](#cite_note-4)

Moishe met Roza in [Vilna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vilna "Vilna"), Russian Empire (now Vilnius, Lithuania), where her father worked as a furrier. She and her family moved to New York because of increasing anti-Jewish sentiment in Russia, changing her first name to Rose. Moishe, faced with compulsory military service if he remained in Russia, moved to America as soon as he could afford to (arrived on August 14, 1890). Once in New York, he changed his first name to Morris. Gershovitz lived with a maternal uncle in [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"), working as a foreman in a women's shoe factory. He married Rose on July 21, 1895, and Gershovitz soon Anglicized his name to Gershwine.[[5]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHyland20031–3-5)[[6]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPollack20063-6)[[7]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJablonski198729–31-7) Their first child, [Ira Gershwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ira_Gershwin "Ira Gershwin"), was born on December 6, 1896, after which the family moved into a second-floor apartment at 242 Snediker Avenue in the [East New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_New_York "East New York") neighborhood of Brooklyn.

### Early life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=George_Gershwin&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early life")]

George was born on September 26, 1898, in the Snediker Avenue apartment. His birth certificate identifies him as Jacob Gershwine, with the surname pronounced "Gershvin" in the [Yiddish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yiddish "Yiddish")-speaking community.[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9) He was named after his grandfather, and, contrary to the American practice, had no middle name. **Theodor Seuss Geisel** ([/suːs ˈɡaɪzəl, zɔɪs -/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English") [ⓘ](/wiki/File:En-us-Geisel.ogg "File:En-us-Geisel.ogg") [*sooss GHY-zəl, zoyss -⁠*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key");[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-DICT-3)[[4]](#cite_note-mw-4) March 2, 1904 – September 24, 1991)[[5]](#cite_note-5) was an American children's author, illustrator, animator, and [cartoonist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartoonist "Cartoonist"). He is known for his work writing and illustrating [more than 60 books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Seuss_bibliography "Dr. Seuss bibliography") under the pen name **Dr. Seuss** ([/suːs, zuːs/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English") [*sooss, zooss*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key")).[[4]](#cite_note-mw-4)[[6]](#cite_note-6) His work includes many of the most popular children's books of all time, selling over 600 million copies and being translated into more than 20 languages by the time of his death.[[7]](#cite_note-Reader-7)

Geisel adopted the name "Dr. Seuss" as an undergraduate at [Dartmouth College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dartmouth_College "Dartmouth College") and as a graduate student at [Lincoln College, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_College,_Oxford "Lincoln College, Oxford"). He left Oxford in 1927 to begin his career as an illustrator and cartoonist for *[Vanity Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanity_Fair_(magazine) "Vanity Fair (magazine)")*, *[Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_(magazine) "Life (magazine)")*, and various other publications. He also worked as an illustrator for [advertising campaigns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertising_campaign "Advertising campaign"), including for [Flit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FLIT "FLIT") and [Standard Oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_Oil "Standard Oil"), and as a [political cartoonist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_cartoon "Political cartoon") for the New York newspaper *[PM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PM_(newspaper) "PM (newspaper)")*. He published his first children's book *[And to Think That I Saw It on Mulberry Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/And_to_Think_That_I_Saw_It_on_Mulberry_Street "And to Think That I Saw It on Mulberry Street")* in 1937. During [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), he took a brief hiatus from children's literature to illustrate political cartoons, and he worked in the animation and film department of the [United States Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army").

After the war, Geisel returned to writing children's books, writing acclaimed works such as *[If I Ran the Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_I_Ran_the_Zoo "If I Ran the Zoo")* (1950), *[Horton Hears a Who!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horton_Hears_a_Who! "Horton Hears a Who!")* (1954), *[The Cat in the Hat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cat_in_the_Hat "The Cat in the Hat")* (1957), *[How the Grinch Stole Christmas!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_the_Grinch_Stole_Christmas! "How the Grinch Stole Christmas!")* (1957), *[Green Eggs and Ham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Eggs_and_Ham "Green Eggs and Ham")* (1960), *[One Fish, Two Fish, Red Fish, Blue Fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Fish,_Two_Fish,_Red_Fish,_Blue_Fish "One Fish, Two Fish, Red Fish, Blue Fish")* (1960), *[The Sneetches and Other Stories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sneetches_and_Other_Stories "The Sneetches and Other Stories")* (1961), *[The Lorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lorax "The Lorax")* (1971), *[The Butter Battle Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Butter_Battle_Book "The Butter Battle Book")* (1984), and *[Oh, the Places You'll Go!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oh,_the_Places_You'll_Go! "Oh, the Places You'll Go!")* (1990). He published over 60 books during his career, which have spawned numerous [adaptations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_adaptation "Film adaptation"), including eleven television specials, five feature films, [a Broadway musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seussical "Seussical"), and four television series.

He received two [Primetime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Awards "Primetime Emmy Awards") for [Outstanding Children's Special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Children's_Program "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Children's Program") for *[Halloween Is Grinch Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halloween_Is_Grinch_Night "Halloween Is Grinch Night")* (1978) and [Outstanding Animated Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Animated_Program "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Animated Program") for *[The Grinch Grinches the Cat in the Hat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Grinch_Grinches_the_Cat_in_the_Hat "The Grinch Grinches the Cat in the Hat")* (1982).[[8]](#cite_note-8) In 1984, he won a [Pulitzer Prize Special Citation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_Special_Citation "Pulitzer Prize Special Citation"). His birthday, March 2, has been adopted as the annual date for [National Read Across America Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Read_Across_America_Day "Read Across America Day"), an initiative focused on reading created by the [National Education Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Education_Association "National Education Association").

## Life and career

### Early years

Geisel was born and raised in [Springfield, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springfield,_Massachusetts "Springfield, Massachusetts"), the son of Theodor Robert Geisel and Henrietta Geisel ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") Seuss).[[9]](#cite_note-ucdsbio-9)[[10]](#cite_note-early-10) His father managed the family brewery and was later appointed to supervise Springfield's public park system by Mayor [John A. Denison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_A._Denison "John A. Denison")[[11]](#cite_note-11) after the brewery closed because of [Prohibition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition_in_the_United_States "Prohibition in the United States").[[12]](#cite_note-beer-12) [Mulberry Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mulberry_Street_(Springfield,_Massachusetts) "Mulberry Street (Springfield, Massachusetts)") in Springfield, made famous in his first children's book *[And to Think That I Saw It on Mulberry Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/And_to_Think_That_I_Saw_It_on_Mulberry_Street "And to Think That I Saw It on Mulberry Street")*, is near his boyhood home on Fairfield Street.[[13]](#cite_note-13) The family was of German descent, and Geisel and his sister Marnie experienced anti-German prejudice from other children following the outbreak of World War I in 1914.[[14]](#cite_note-14) Geisel was raised as a [Missouri Synod Lutheran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lutheran_Church–Missouri_Synod "Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod") and remained in the denomination his entire life.[[15]](#cite_note-stltoday2012-15)

Geisel was educated at Dartmouth College, graduating in 1925.[[16]](#cite_note-16) At Dartmouth, he joined the [Sigma Phi Epsilon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigma_Phi_Epsilon "Sigma Phi Epsilon") fraternity[[9]](#cite_note-ucdsbio-9) and the humor magazine *[Dartmouth Jack-O-Lantern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dartmouth_Jack-O-Lantern "Dartmouth Jack-O-Lantern")*, eventually rising to the rank of editor-in-chief.[[9]](#cite_note-ucdsbio-9) While at Dartmouth, he was caught drinking [gin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gin "Gin") with nine friends in his room.[[17]](#cite_note-17) At the time, the possession and consumption of alcohol was illegal under [Prohibition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition_in_the_United_States "Prohibition in the United States") laws, which remained in place between 1920 and 1933. From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

American music award

The **Grammy Trustees Award** is awarded by [The Recording Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Recording_Academy "The Recording Academy") to individuals who, during their careers in music, technology, and so on have made significant contributions, other than performance, to the field of recording.[[1]](#cite_note-1) From 1983 onwards, performers could also receive this award. This award is distinct from the [Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Lifetime_Achievement_Award "Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award"), which honors performers.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

The **Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award** is a special [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") presented by [The Recording Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Recording_Academy "The Recording Academy") to "performers who, during their lifetimes, have made creative contributions of outstanding artistic significance to the field of recording."[[1]](#cite_note-1)

This award is distinct from the [Grammy Hall of Fame Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Hall_of_Fame_Award "Grammy Hall of Fame Award"), which honors specific recordings rather than individuals, and the [Grammy Trustees Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Trustees_Award "Grammy Trustees Award"), which honors contributions other than performance.

The honor was established in 1962, with the first awarded recipient in [1963](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "5th Annual Grammy Awards").

**Copland** is an [impact crater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") on [Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(planet) "Mercury (planet)"). Its floor is flooded with volcanic smooth plains material, which could be related to the activity that formed the nearby bright vent known as [Nathair Facula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathair_Facula "Nathair Facula").

## Naming

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Copland_(crater)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Naming")]

Amateur astronomer Ronald Dantowitz and his colleagues Scott Teare and Marek Kozubal used the Mt. Wilson 60-inch telescope in 1998 to observe a very bright feature on this portion of Mercury's surface, and they assumed that the bright feature was an impact crater. Mr. Dantowitz expressed his wish that the crater be named "Copland" (after American composer [Aaron Copland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Copland "Aaron Copland")) once better images of the area were obtained from spacecraft.

Surprisingly, *[MESSENGER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MESSENGER "MESSENGER")* images from Mercury flyby 3 revealed that the small bright feature, seen at the left edge of this image and now known as [Nathair Facula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathair_Facula "Nathair Facula"), is not an [impact crater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") but more closely resembles a [volcanic vent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcanic_vent "Volcanic vent"). No convention for naming volcanic vents on Mercury had yet been adopted, because none were identified prior to *MESSENGER*'s first Mercury flyby. A *MESSENGER* team member corresponded with Mr. Dantowitz and suggested that the name Copland be proposed instead for a large crater nearby. He agreed, and the [International Astronomical Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union") (IAU) approved the name Copland on March 3, 2010.[[1]](#cite_note-1)[[2]](#cite_note-IAU-2)

**Stravinsky** is a [crater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") on [Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(planet) "Mercury (planet)"). It overlays the rim of the much older [Vyāsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vyāsa_(crater) "Vyāsa (crater)") crater. It was named by the [IAU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union") in 1979 for the influential Russian composer [Igor Stravinsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Stravinsky "Igor Stravinsky").[[1]](#cite_note-1) The crater was first imaged by [Mariner 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariner_10 "Mariner 10") in 1974.[[2]](#cite_note-Davies_1978-2)

To the north of Stravinsky is the crater [Rubens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubens_(crater) "Rubens (crater)"), and to the southwest is [Vyāsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vyāsa_(crater) "Vyāsa (crater)").

**Stravinsky** is a [crater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") on [Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(planet) "Mercury (planet)"). It overlays the rim of the much older [Vyāsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vyāsa_(crater) "Vyāsa (crater)") crater. It was named by the [IAU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union") in 1979 for the influential Russian composer [Igor Stravinsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Stravinsky "Igor Stravinsky").[[1]](#cite_note-1) The crater was first imaged by [Mariner 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariner_10 "Mariner 10") in 1974.[[2]](#cite_note-Davies_1978-2)

To the north of Stravinsky is the crater [Rubens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubens_(crater) "Rubens (crater)"), and to the southwest is [Vyāsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vyāsa_(crater) "Vyāsa (crater)").

# Disney (crater)

![}](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Disney-crater.png/330px-Disney-crater.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)
![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Disney_crater_labeled_by_NASA.png/250px-Disney_crater_labeled_by_NASA.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)

**Disney** is an [impact crater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater") in the H-15 (Bach) Quadrangle of [Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(planet) "Mercury (planet)").[[1]](#cite_note-1) It was approved and adopted by the [IAU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Astronomical_Union "International Astronomical Union") on Dec 19, 2012.[[2]](#cite_note-2) Disney is 113 km (70 mi) in diameter. This crater was named after [Walt Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney "Walt Disney") (Walter Elias), the American entrepreneur, voice actor, film producer, and animator. Disney is one of many craters named after notable art figures; per the [Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_Group_for_Planetary_System_Nomenclature "Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature"), Mercury's craters are all named after a famous artist, composer, or writer who was influential for more than 50 years and deceased for more than three years at the time the crater was named.[[3]](#cite_note-3) Disney was named months after [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") acknowledged it for its resemblance to [Mickey Mouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mickey_Mouse "Mickey Mouse").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
